title: Chicken Francaise
description: It is thought that Chicken Francaise, also known as Francese, was created in America by Italian immigrants. As with numerous Italian chicken dishes, they were originally intended for veal but taste equally as good with chicken. But back to the name, why an American Italian dish is called “French”, maybe it’s because of all the butter, maybe the wine, but one thing for sure, the flavours are superb! Enjoy it with a rich and dry white wine or a light red such as Gamay or Pinot Noir.
ingredients: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, butterflied and flattened, then salted
1 cup white wine (click for wine alternatives)
directions: Crack the eggs into a large enough dish to fit chicken breast. Season eggs with salt and pepper, give them a light beat. Add Parmesan cheese and half of the chopped parsley to the egg-wash, mix well.
Add the plain flour to a plate.
To a frying pan on moderate heat, add the olive oil, half the butter, and the smashed garlic clove.
Coat the chicken in the flour, shake off any excess flour.
Dip the chicken in the egg wash, make sure it’s totally covered and place in hot oil.
Cook chicken for 3-4 minutes each side (depending on thickness). Flip over once brown and cook the other side. Transfer chicken to a hot plate and rest.

To the same frying pan, add the white wine, deglazing the pan. Add the crushed garlic, the juice of half a lemon, the chicken stock, and the remainder of chopped parsley. Add the remainder of butter and reduce for 2 minutes or so on full heat.
Return the chicken to the sauce and continue heating chicken on medium heat. Serve the chicken with the reduced, thickened sauce.
